dedupe_keys.name: national and subnational estimates of agricultural residues organic municipal waste and used cooking oil in nigeria kenya and south africa

description: These tables estimate how much organic waste Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa produce, region by region, as feedstock for plants that turn waste into fuels and chemicals. The producers are Raymond Atughwe, Siddharth Gadkari and Michael Short of the University of Surrey. Coverage is three feedstocks, namely crop residues, the organic fraction of municipal solid waste and used cooking oil, at national level and for states in Nigeria, counties in Kenya and provinces in South Africa, in 15 tables. The latest version revised several estimates to match the method in the associated study and supersedes earlier releases, and the record links to three related deposits from the same work. The tables are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: figures are modelled estimates from generation rates and statistics, not measured collection, the organic waste share depends on assumed waste composition, and the method is set out in the paper, not the deposit. Simulation uses: siting and sizing composting, anaerobic digestion or biorefinery plants, and modelling organic waste collection and supply chains in African cities and regions. Related records: the What a Waste database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) gives national waste composition, and SWOLFPy (model-swolfpy) models waste system options.
